newsitem.title: USA: UPS, Teamsters meeting with federal negotiator.
newsitem.headline: UPS, Teamsters meeting with federal negotiator.

text.p: United Parcel Service and the Teamsters union meet for last-ditch talks Thursday with a federal negotiator, who said that at this late date every step to avoid a strike is "like climbing a mountain."
The two sides met only hours ahead of a strike deadline that threatens to cripple the biggest package carrier in the United States at midnight.

The two sides met briefly at the Washington Court Hotel, where the Teamsters are headquartered, before leaving for talks at an undisclosed location with the head of the Federal Mediation and Conciliation Service, John Calhoun Wells.
"Time is getting short, there's only a few hours left," Wells said. "Both sides have agreed to my request to meet face to face. At this late stage, every step is like climbing a mountain."
But Teamsters President Ron Carey said he was determined to try to reach an agreement, saying: "We're here to negotiate a contract, not a strike."
